commit.message:
python: Remove dependency on requests and charset_normalizer

Both of these are completely unused, even transitively

docs: Update token requirements to include read:org

The new team reviewers functionality requires additional
read:org permissions to get the available teams.

It would be too confusing to make this optional, so require it
and update the docs.

build: Rename types to core_types to avoid stdlib shadow

This file could potentially shadow python's own types module,
so rename it to core_types.

github: Rework GraphQL batching and error handling to salvage partial work

Restructure the GitHub GraphQL layer around a flat, resizable query so that
partial results are never thrown away and failed work is re-transacted
precisely.

GraphqlQuery now holds a heterogeneous list of aliased fields (SingleQuery)
with stable per-prefix alias indices, so it can split() in half or subset()
to arbitrary fields without result aliases colliding. GithubQuery subclasses
it with the repo-specific field builders and result parsers.

endpoint.graphql no longer raises on GraphQL field errors. It returns a
GraphqlResponse carrying partial data plus per-field errors, and only raises
for a request error (200 with no data) or a non-retryable HTTP status. Retry
backoff is now driven by GitHub's headers, honoring Retry-After and waiting
out an exhausted rate-limit budget, and retries secondary-limit (403) as well
as transient 5xx.

Also recover a PR's id via a head-ref lookup when a create comes back
"already exists", so a later update never targets an empty id, and log the
remaining rate-limit budget at the end of a verbose run.

git: Use -z for null separated parsing

Some git commands using paths will escape unicode characters, which
we then don't handle properly.

Fix this by passing -z so git doesn't escape these, and splitting on nulls.

Add a test

amend: Fix last-touched when deleting files

Previously deleted files were not affected by this replay
logic because they don't show up in the new index.

Fix this by adding the old version of the deleted file to
the base of the merge, so the merge-tree will treat it as
deleted. Add a test for this.

amend: Fix last-touched functionality

last-touched will amend the file into the correct
commit, but incorrectly then removes the changes immediately
when replaying the rest of the stack on top. This was not
caught by tests because those only checked the exact commit
and file, without checking that the rest of the stack is
correct.

Fix this by reimplementing with the merge-tree engine, which
is more modern and faster anyway. Update tests to catch this case.

build: Move manpage logic into a shell script

This makes it easier to reuse across potential build systems.

Also move version into version.py so that it doesn't intercept init.py.

config: Use interpolation=None

configparser includes an interpolation feature where keys can
specify replacement with other keys. This is not necessary for us
and breaks keys with literal %, so turn it off.

build: Keep .coverage file out of repo root

Running make test drops a file in repo root. Move that to
build/.

git: Don't crash on a whitespace only commit msg

Currently we expect at least one nonws line of text per commit
message to act as the title. That may not be the case (git allows
empty commit messages). We do not want to crash if one of these
appears in the stack.

shell: Don't crash when decoding invalid output

git output can include invalid bytes, so we want to
leniently smooth the output instead of crashing.

This can happen on the conflict dump path if a file
contains invalid bytes.

python: Add support for 3.13, 3.14

Newer versions of python are now available, make sure we support them.
git: Delete unused regex variables

- Fixed the github issues when reordering PRs in a stack
- Patchsets now uses git merge-tree, and will be much more accurate within a single file

Minor improvements:
- QOL improvements for "config"
- Various other qol fixes

* lint: Fix misc pylint file warnings by @jerry-skydio in https://github.com/Skydio/revup/pull/195
* git: Add option for no_config in git shell by @jerry-skydio in https://github.com/Skydio/revup/pull/188
* git: Use merge-tree in patchsets by @jerry-skydio in https://github.com/Skydio/revup/pull/187
* upload: Allow relative between different uploaders by @jerry-skydio in https://github.com/Skydio/revup/pull/205
* git: Don't swallow all push output by @jerry-skydio in https://github.com/Skydio/revup/pull/204
* upload: Check PRs merge into base branch rather than base ref by @jerry-skydio in https://github.com/Skydio/revup/pull/207
* config: Improve input checking in config command by @jerry-skydio in https://github.com/Skydio/revup/pull/209
* config: Remove -nx negation shortform by @jerry-skydio in https://github.com/Skydio/revup/pull/210
* upload: Push a dummy commit to work around reordering issues by @jerry-skydio in https://github.com/Skydio/revup/pull/208
* upload: Query head oid of a PR via commits by @jerry-skydio in https://github.com/Skydio/revup/pull/206

## New Contributors
* @f440 made their first contribution in https://github.com/Skydio/revup/pull/194

data.name: Release of ARMI 0.6.4
data.body:
Release Date: 2026-03-25

This was a very short-burn release. The biggest new feature is the addition of matProps, the materials library. This
tool allows developers to flexibly define materials with properties in several flexible ways. This release also included
a lot of clean up work, such as moving several parameters and settings out of ARMI. The HistoryTracker EOL interaction
was optimized. And a block converter was added for mixed-pin assemblies.

Code Changes, Features
----------------------
- [PR#2453](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2453) Adding matProps: a material library
- [PR#2405](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2405) Remove ruamel.yaml dependency pin maximum
- [PR#2436](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2436) Optimizing the HistoryTracker EOL interaction
- [PR#2442](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2442) Defaulting the Database to read mode
- [PR#2477](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2477) Adding a block converter for mixed pin assemblies
- [PR#2478](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2478) Checking for unrepresented XS IDs
- [PR#2479](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2479) Adding method to DefaultExecuter for final parameter updates


Code Changes, Bugs and Fixes
----------------------------
- [PR#2468](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2468) Fixing shuffle file reading in reload runs
- [PR#2470](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2470) Removing unused and broken material UThZr


Code Changes, Maintenance, or Trivial
-------------------------------------
- [PR#2422](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2422) Removing unused parameter fluxAdjPeak
- [PR#2430](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2430) Moving 27 TH parameters out of ARMI
- [PR#2451](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2451) Moving 7 Neutronics Settings out of ARMI
- [PR#2456](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2456) Anonymizing example user names in IPYNBs
- [PR#2457](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2457) Doing misc cleanup and temporary pyDOE issue
- [PR#2458](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2458) Removing broken pyDOE dep and LatinHyperCubeSuiteBuilder
- [PR#2459](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2459) Removing Core.getAssembliesOfType in favor of iterChildrenWithFlags
- [PR#2460](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2460) Stopping intermittent CI failures
- [PR#2461](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2461) Renaming _Material_Test to AbstractMaterialTest
- [PR#2462](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2462) Switching from coveralls.io to codecov.io
- [PR#2482](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2482) Ensuring codecov.io does not fail if coverage drops a tiny amount
- [PR#2483](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2483) Producing an ARMI wheel with every merge to main


Documentation-Only Changes
--------------------------
- [PR#2441](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2441) Moving the README text up in the PDF ToC
- [PR#2481](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2481) Getting nuclide_demo tutorial working again
- [PR#2443](https://github.com/terrapower/armi/pull/2443) Starting release cycle for ARMI 0.6.4

commit.message:
Add comprehensive GIS tools and ease-of-use features (#519)

* Reposition docs and homepage as "the animation studio for maps"

Rewrite homepage hero, use cases, gallery descriptions, and CTA to
emphasize what makes Noodles unique: timeline-first animation, reactive
pipelines, and cinema-quality GPU rendering. Add a new Positioning
section between gallery and video. Rewrite intro.md to lead with the
animation differentiator. Completely overhaul comparison.md with
detailed head-to-head tables against Kepler, After Effects, D3, QGIS,
and Flourish.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add basemap gallery with 35 searchable styles (Phase 1A)

Add a searchable, filterable basemap gallery dialog to the MapStyle
field. Users can now click a gallery icon next to the URL input to
browse ~35 curated basemaps from Carto, OpenFreeMap, Stadia, Protomaps,
ESRI, NASA, and OpenStreetMap — with search, provider filter, and
category filter (street/light/dark/imagery/terrain/artistic).

Raster tile sources (ESRI, NASA, OSM) are auto-wrapped into valid
MapLibre style objects via rasterUrlToStyle().

- New: BasemapGallery component (Radix dialog, CSS module)
- New: Expanded BASEMAP_CATALOG with typed entries in map-styles.ts
- Modified: MapStyleFieldComponent gains a gallery button (pi-images)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Enhance data importer with URL loading and GeoJSON detection (Phase 2A)

- Add URL text input below drop zone for loading remote data files
- Detect GeoJSON format from file extension or content inspection
- Create GeoJsonLayerOp pipeline for .geojson files instead of ScatterplotLayerOp
- Accept .geojson and .tsv file extensions in the file picker
- Add CSS for URL input section

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Auto-detect coordinate columns in CSV imports

When a CSV is imported, inspect the header row to find common
coordinate column names (longitude/latitude, lon/lat, lng/lat, x/y)
and generate the correct AccessorOp expression automatically.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add Layer Panel with visibility and opacity controls (Phase 4A)

New sidebar tab alongside the node tree that lists all layers
connected to a DeckRenderer. Each layer has:
- Eye icon to toggle visibility
- Click to select and navigate to the layer node
- Opacity slider for quick adjustment

Adds a tabbed sidebar container (Nodes | Layers) so users can
manage layers without touching the node graph.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add sample datasets to data importer for quick onboarding

One-click loading of curated public datasets (World Countries,
US States, World Airports, World Cities) to help new users
get data on the map instantly without needing their own files.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add inline Style Panel to Layer Panel (Phase 4B)

Click a layer to expand its style editor inline — color pickers,
sliders, and toggles for the most important visual properties.
Supports ScatterplotLayer, PathLayer, ArcLayer, GeoJsonLayer,
PolygonLayer, HeatmapLayer, ColumnLayer, H3HexagonLayer, IconLayer,
and TextLayer.

Also adds "show in graph" button per layer to navigate to the node.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add Measure Tool for distance and area calculations (Phase 1B)

Floating dialog with distance/area modes, unit conversion
(km, miles, meters, nautical miles), per-segment breakdown,
and spherical area calculation. Add points by coordinates,
with live total display.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add comprehensive GIS tools: geometry ops, spatial analysis, format support, and GeoEditor

Adds 30+ new operators covering geometry operations (Buffer, Union, Difference,
Intersect, Centroid, ConvexHull, Voronoi, Dissolve, Clip, transforms),
spatial analysis (SpatialJoin, PointInPolygon, NearestPoint, clustering, interpolation),
grid generation (Point/Hex/Square), format support (GeoParquet, Shapefile, PMTiles, XYZ),
and a GeoEditor operator with visual drawing dialog. Includes 51 passing tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add grouped GIS tool menu and guided wizards to the tools shelf

The ~35 GIS operators added previously had no discoverable entry point. This
adds a declarative recipe registry, one generic wizard that can drive any
recipe, a searchable grouped dropdown, and a one-off Draw tool.

Every recipe produces real nodes: the wizard's answers become serialized
operator inputs, and the parameter node is selected and framed after creation
so it is obvious where to change values later.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address PR review: SQL quoting, GeoEditor state, comparison tone

Greptile P1s:
- GeoParquetOp interpolated the URL and geometry column straight into SQL, so a
  value containing a quote broke the query. Added sqlLiteral/sqlIdentifier
  helpers (with tests) and floor the LIMIT.
- GeoEditorDialog accepted a 2-click polygon, producing a 3-position ring.
  Polygons now require 3 points; the Finish button and counter follow suit.
- Dialog features were initialized once, so reopening could save stale geometry
  over a newer upstream value. Now re-reads the operator on each open.

Chris's docs notes: Kepler/FSQ Studio has time-filter video export and DuckDB
SQL (expressions are Enterprise-only); AE comparison is against AE+GeoLayers;
GeoLibre has trips-layer playback; time-to-first-viz is honest about the
learning curve; called out that import-after-analysis should be easy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add drop-to-import on the graph canvas

Dropping a data file anywhere on the canvas now builds its pipeline at the drop
point, without opening the Import Data dialog first. This is the follow-up Chris
asked about: making import-after-analysis as easy as possible.

Extracted the dialog's pipeline construction into import-pipelines.ts, a pure
module with no React or store dependency, and moved the write-then-scaffold
sequence into a useFileImport hook shared by the dialog and the canvas.

Fixed along the way:
- The CSV pipeline wired three edges to a /deck node it never created, so an
  import into an empty project produced a layer connected to nothing. A test now
  asserts every edge endpoint is a node the builder actually creates.
- Shapefile, GeoParquet and PMTiles were reachable as operators but not as
  imports. All three now have detection, a source operator and a pipeline, and
  binary formats round-trip as a Blob instead of being read as text.
- BoundingBox was wired to GeoJSON sources, which it can't read; it only accepts
  point arrays, so it's now wired for tabular sources only.

Replaced data-importer-tool.test.ts, which re-implemented the builder inline and
asserted against its own copy, with 19 tests against the real module.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Surface the GIS tools in the real menu bar

The tools shelf was never rendered. Nothing imported tools-shelf.tsx, on
this branch or on main, so the Draw button, the Measure tool and the
grouped GIS tools dropdown were all unreachable. The buttons users
actually see live in the centerSection of top-menu-bar.tsx.

Move the new entries there and delete the orphaned shelf so there is only
one place that renders these tools.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Make upload button shorter

* Flatten the tool shelf and move Draw/Measure onto the map

The shelf hid every recipe category behind one "GIS Tools" dropdown, and Draw
and Measure opened coordinate-entry dialogs instead of letting you point at the
map. This reworks both.

Shelf:
- Import Data is a split button: the main half opens the importer, the caret
  lists every source format.
- Recipe groups (Geometry, Combine, Analysis, Transform, Grids) sit at the top
  level and collapse into a "More" ellipsis menu as the window narrows. The
  overflow point comes from measuring real button widths in a hidden row, so
  computeVisibleCount is pure and testable.
- More always offers search across all recipes.
- Add Op moved to the far right, where an escape hatch belongs.

Map tools:
- Draw and Measure now arm useMapToolStore instead of opening a dialog. The
  shelf button stays lit while armed.
- MapToolOverlay captures clicks on the real map, unprojects them through the
  live camera, and paints in-progress geometry as SVG. The measurement readout
  tracks the pointer, so the number moves before you commit a vertex.
- Escape cancels then disarms, Enter finishes, Backspace undoes a vertex.
- "Add to graph" routes drawings and measurements through a GeoEditor node, so
  the geometry stays keyframeable.

Deletes measure-tool, draw-geometry-tool and geo-tool-menu, all now unreachable.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Project map tools through the canvas box and de-overlap added nodes

Two problems, both from assuming a coordinate space that does not hold.

Map tool projection: the overlay converted client coordinates using its own
bounding rect, but maplibre projects against its canvas, which is a different
box. react-map-gl renders children inside a wrapper div, and in fixed display
mode the canvas is sized to the render resolution and letterboxed inside the
pane. At scale 1 with the map filling the window the two boxes coincided, which
is why it looked right; in split view the offset and scale diverge and clicks
land well away from the pointer. Conversion now routes through the canvas rect
and its CSS size, in both directions. The maths moved to overlay-coords.ts so it
is covered by tests rather than only by looking at it.

Node placement: every tool that scaffolds a pipeline placed nodes at a fixed
offset from the viewport centre, so a second import dropped straight on top of
the first. resolveNodeOverlaps shifts a newly built group down as a rigid block
until it clears the existing graph, preserving the left-to-right shape each
builder deliberately produces. Applied to file import, the recipe wizard, the
point wizard and the map tools. Nodes inside containers are left alone, since
they are positioned relative to a parent that moves with them.

* Make the More menu hold only what overflowed the shelf

More listed every category regardless of what was already on the shelf, so
Geometry appeared both as its own button and inside More. It also rendered
unconditionally, which meant a wide window showed a More button holding a copy
of the row next to it.

More now appears only when a category could not fit, and lists only the
categories that were pushed out. Search still spans every recipe: once the user
types a name they want it found wherever it currently lives.

Deciding this needs two fit passes, because the two answers depend on each
other. More occupies width, but it only exists if something overflowed, so
reserving its space up front would cut a category that would otherwise have fit
exactly. computeShelfLayout checks the no-More fit first and only re-fits
against the narrower space when something is genuinely left over.

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
fix: container scope-boundary bugs (copy-paste, delete cascade, undo/redo) (#503)

* fix: container copy-paste now includes GraphInputOp/GraphOutputOp children

Container children use path-based nesting (ID prefix), not ReactFlow's
parentId. The copy logic was looking for children via parentId and
toObject() (which only returns currently displayed nodes), so container
children in a different scope were silently dropped during copy.

Extracts copy-paste logic into shared utilities (copy-paste-utils.ts)
that both production code and tests import, eliminating the parallel
re-implementation that previously allowed test/production drift.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: address review feedback on copy-paste utilities

- collectContainerChildren now recurses into nested containers so all
  descendants are collected (fixes silent drop of nested container children)
- collectGroupParents is now pure — no longer mutates the input Set
- identifyContainerChildren builds reverse map once instead of O(n²) scan
- Add unit test for recursive nested container collection

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: cascade delete to path-based container children

Deleting a ContainerOp now also removes all path-based children
(GraphInputOp, GraphOutputOp, nested ops) and their edges. Previously,
only the container node itself was removed, leaving orphaned children
and dangling edges in the graph state.

Both deletion paths are fixed:
- deleteElements (programmatic deletion)
- handleNodesDeleted (keyboard Delete via ReactFlow onNodesDelete)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: extract expandDeleteSet utility with tests

Extracts the cascade-delete logic into a shared pure function so both
deleteElements and handleNodesDeleted call the same code path, and it
can be tested directly without React hook infrastructure.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: undo/redo captures full graph state including container children

The undo system previously captured snapshots from ReactFlow's internal
store, which only contains displayedNodes (current scope). Container
children exist outside that scope, so they were lost on undo.

Now passes getFullNodes/getFullEdges to the undo system so it captures
and restores the complete graph state, not just the visible scope.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: unify nodesRef/edgesRef into single graphRef

Replaces the two separate refs and their useEffect sync with a single
graphRef assigned directly during render. Consumers (CopyControls,
UndoRedoHandler, useNodeDropOnEdge, findEdgeAtPosition) now receive one
ref prop instead of individual getter functions.

Direct assignment during render eliminates the stale-ref window that
existed with the useEffect pattern — the ref is always current.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: add container scope operations tests for cascading bugs

Tests the class of bugs where operations must cascade across container
scope boundaries. Covers: delete cascading to children, copy collecting
out-of-scope children, undo restoring full state, and the invariant
that no orphaned children exist after any operation.

Models the displayedNodes vs full-nodes split to verify that code
operating on the full graph (via graphRef) works correctly even though
ReactFlow only sees the current scope.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: clarify displayedNodes vs hidden in test comments

ReactFlow receives a filtered subset via controlled mode, not hidden
nodes. Children are excluded entirely from ReactFlow's store.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: redistribute scope-boundary tests to proper homes and add CopyControls component test

Delete the monolithic container-scope-operations.test.tsx and move its
valuable tests to where they belong: transform-graph cascade deletion to
transform-graph.test.ts, orphan invariants to copy-paste-utils.test.ts.
Add new component-level test for CopyControls proving it reads from
graphRef (would break if wiring reverted). Fix undo-redo graphRef test.

Includes a noodles.json with nested containers and a README with

and undo/redo across scope boundaries.

fix: improve Point2D/Vec3 table cell editing and wire up geocoder (#502)

* fix: replace InputNumber with plain text inputs in Point2D/Vec3 table cell editors

PrimeReact's InputNumber was aggressively reformatting values, rounding to
limited precision, blocking context menu paste, and requiring double-entry
to commit values. Switch to DraggableNumberCellInput (plain <input type="text">)
which allows natural decimal typing and immediate value propagation. Also wires
up the GeocodingDialog for Point2D cells that have geocoder enabled.

* style: remove stray blank line in table-editor CSS

* fix: cell preview not updating after geocoder selection

The handleComplete closure captured stale state when onChange and
onComplete were called in the same synchronous flow (e.g. from the
geocoder). Use a ref to track the latest value so updateData always
receives the current value regardless of React's batching.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* style: move GeocodingDialog import after third-party imports

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: prevent blur race when clicking geocoder button

Adding onMouseDown preventDefault to the geocoder button prevents the

commit.message:
Fix node disappearing when title input is blurred without changes (#518)

Fixes a bug where nodes would disappear from the canvas after:
1. Double-clicking a node header to edit the title
2. Clicking into the title input (without changing the text)
3. Clicking on the background to blur the input

The issue was caused by updateId() calling updateOperatorId() even when
the name hadn't changed. This triggered an unnecessary ID "update" where
newQualifiedId === nodeId, which caused React Flow to re-render the node
while queueing deletion of the operator in a microtask. During the
re-render, the displayedNodes memo would recalculate and the operator
would be deleted mid-reconciliation, leaving the node in an inconsistent
state.

The fix adds a guard clause to skip calling updateOperatorId when the
trimmed name matches the current baseName, preventing the unnecessary
update cycle entirely.

Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Blender-style multi-input handles with order-correct data flow (#120)

* Fix Node Properties sidebar for multi inputs (broken from par/out change) and add multi input handles

* show base name instead of fully qualified path on the input handle

* attempt to fix slots

* attempt to follow @peterkogo advice

* distinguish handle ids

* Add multi-input order utilities with edge-array order as single source of truth

Edge array order now defines connection order for ListField multi-inputs.
normalizeMultiInputEdges derives orderIndex/groupSize caches from it, and
ListField.setConnectionOrder (replacing reorderInputs) idempotently syncs
the field's Map order from edge ids. Removes dead slotIndex handle parsing,
the broken opMap migration effect, and the uncompilable node-properties test
(rewrite forthcoming).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Sync ListField connection order to edge-array order in transformGraph

addConnection early-returns for existing ids and appends new ones at the Map
end, so reused operators kept stale order whenever edges were inserted
mid-group or the array was reordered. Every transformGraph run now re-asserts
Map order == edge array order.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Rewrite multi-input interaction layer around edge-array order

onConnect inserts at the slot tracked during the drag and syncs ListField
order in the same update; a new onReconnect implements Blender-style
drag-to-reorder on the canvas (same-handle drops reorder, source swaps keep
their slot, cross-handle moves disconnect and reconnect atomically via
replaceEdgeId). All edge mutations (delete, node delete, AI edits, node-drop-
on-edge, sidebar reorder) renormalize through normalizeMultiInputEdges, and
the transformGraph effect re-derives slot caches as a catch-all for undo/redo
and paste. Also replaces xyflow reconnectEdge in the single-input path, which
was silently rewriting edge ids to xy-edge__ format.

pendingInsertionIndex is now consume-once (takePendingInsertionIndex) and
cleared on cancelled drags via onConnectEnd/onReconnectEnd.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Rewrite MultiInputHandle with flow-coordinate slot math and shared geometry

The insertion index previously read connection.toY (a field that doesn't exist
on ConnectionState) and mixed it with screen-space DOM rects, so drop position
tracking never worked. It now derives the handle center from useInternalNode's
measured handle bounds and the pointer from connection.to — both in flow
coordinates, correct at any zoom. Edge anchors and handle slots share
slotOffsetY, centering the edge fan on the grown handle instead of drifting
below it. Store subscriptions are selector-based so the handle only re-renders

commit.message:
fix(cache): harden endpoint-info cache path against apiserver throttling (#860)

* fix(cache): harden endpoint-info cache path against apiserver throttling

- async task submission fetches only the endpoint record; drops the infra-state
  read whose k8s fallback ran per-request on cache miss
- singleflight: concurrent cache-miss infra reads for the same endpoint coalesce
  into one k8s fetch per process (shielded from awaiter cancellation)
- cacher: loop survives failed iterations instead of exiting; readiness gated on
  a successful loop; image-cache daemonset writes no longer fail the refresh
- cacher TTL: default 600s (was 60s, shorter than a slow refresh loop), exposed
  as chart value cacher.ttlSeconds
- bulk cacher LISTs use resource_version="0" (apiserver watch cache instead of
  quorum etcd reads)

Incident 2026-08-04: high async-task volume + TTL < loop duration pushed all
gateway replicas to per-request label-selector configmap LISTs, saturating the
ml-serving-new apiserver read pool (APF 429s cluster-wide); a 429 on the
image-cache write also crash-looped the cacher.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cache): address review findings on cacher readiness and coalesced-task exceptions

- drop the readiness file when a cache loop iteration fails, so persistent
  failures surface as NotReady now that the process no longer exits
- retrieve and log the coalesced infra-state task's exception when every
  awaiter was cancelled before consuming it
- trim a dated incident reference from a code comment

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
feat(chart): opt-in securityContext on model-engine db-init Job (#857)

* feat(chart): opt-in securityContext on model-engine db-init Job

The database-setup pre-upgrade hook Job hardcoded no securityContext, so it
cannot run under PodSecurity `restricted` (admission rejects it for
runAsNonRoot, seccompProfile, drop-ALL, allowPrivilegeEscalation). Wire the
same `{{- with .Values.podSecurityContext }}` / `.Values.containerSecurityContext`
guards the gateway/builder/cacher deployments already use, so the Job gets a
securityContext only when those values are set. With them unset (the default,
commented out in values.yaml) the Job renders identically — no change for any
existing deployment. Bump chart 0.2.7 -> 0.2.8.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(chart): also harden the db-migration hook Job securityContext

Extends the same guarded {{- with .Values.podSecurityContext }} /
containerSecurityContext blocks to database_migration_job.yaml. Like db-init,
it's a pre-install,pre-upgrade hook Job with no securityContext, so
db.runDbMigrationScript=true would block installs on PodSecurity `restricted`
clusters. Default (values unset) renders identically; only opt-in consumers
harden. Addresses PR review feedback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
